steps.content: checkPassword builds a 32-element char array by reordering characters from the input; the target string and the flag contain the same characters in a different order.
steps.evidence: a new char array is created with a length that is equal to the compared string at the end. The string being created and compared to the string literal at the end of the method will use the same characters, but the characters will be in a different order.

steps.content: Manually traced each loop iteration on paper to map which input index writes to which buffer index.
steps.evidence: It is important to have either a pen and paper or a separate tab open to step through this challenge as writing the characters being added to the array is the easiest way to visualize the flag as it is being built.

steps.content: Loop 1 (i=0..7): copies the first 8 characters of the target string into buffer[0..7] in order.
steps.evidence: In the first for loop, the first 8 characters of the string are added to the first 8 indices of the new char array, in order.

steps.content: Loop 2 (i=8..15): copies target string indices 15 down to 8 into buffer[8..15], reversing that 8-character block.
steps.evidence: the character the char array is being assigned from the string literal is starting from the 15th index and going down to the 8th index.

steps.content: Loop 3 (i=16,18,...,30): fills even buffer indices with characters at position 46-i in the target string.
steps.evidence: this loop will step through the indices by 2, filling in the remaining even indices (from 16 to 30) within the array with the characters at the [ 46 - i ] index in the string.

steps.content: Loop 4 (i=31,29,...,17): fills odd buffer indices with the character at the same index in the target string.
steps.evidence: the remaining odd indices are filled in by iterating from 31 to 17. The characters being added at each index in the array are the characters at the same index within the starting string.

steps.content: Applying all four loop mappings to the target string produces the flag.
steps.evidence: After performing all of the above operations on the string given at the end of the method, the flag has been built.
